title: Manhole surcharge onto a sloping street
description: A 0.6 m pipe delivers 0.5 m³/s to a manhole with no outlet, which surcharges onto a 10 m wide street sloping at 0.005 (Manning n = 0.02). At steady state the manhole passes the whole inflow onto the street, and downstream the street carries it as uniform sheet flow at the exact normal depth (n q / √S)^(3/5) = 77.7 mm.

citations.title: The urban inundated area: a coupled 1D/2D model for the interaction between sewer and surface
Experimental calibration and validation of sewer/surface flow exchange equations in steady and unsteady flow conditions

expected_states.derivation: At steady state the manhole has no outlet but the street, so it must pass the full pipe inflow (continuity).
Uniform sheet flow of q = Q/B = 0.05 m²/s on slope 0.005 with Manning n = 0.02 (hydraulic radius = depth in 2D shallow-water models): h = (n q / √S)^(3/5).

criteria.rationale: Steady manhole outflow within 1 % of the inflow.
Street depth 75–125 m below the manhole within 3 mm (4 %) of normal depth: the sheet must carry exactly what the manhole released.

By the end of the run, the water stored on the surface and in the pipes has changed by exactly what came in minus what went out. A coupling that moves water between the two models must not make or lose any; each engine's own continuity error is allowed within this limit.

convergence.not_applicable: Scored on exact states that follow from conservation (exchanged and discharged volumes, settled levels): they do not depend on the grid.
